## About Balor Games
Balor Games is a "Triple I" independent game publisher dedicated to long-term stewardship of high-quality creative works. Formed by former leaders of Humble Games, Balor Games oversees an expansive catalog of acclaimed indie games, following the acquisition of the Humble Games and Firestoke catalogs.
Balor Games aims to serve as a cultural curator for independent games, while providing expertise, resources, and belief-driven support to visionary developers.
Position Intro:
Balor Games is looking for a QA Portfolio Manager to own quality assurance strategy and execution across our published portfolio. In this role, you'll be the primary point of accountability for QA coverage on titles developed by multiple external developer teams, and you'll manage the outside QA vendors (FQA, CQA, LQA, compatibility) who deliver that coverage. You'll set testing strategy and standards, scope and book vendor engagements against title milestones, and be the escalation point when quality issues put a release at risk. You’ll also step in for hands-on testing when needed, confirming bug severity, verifying fixes, and writing clear, actionable bug reports. You'll work cross-functionally with Production, Publishing Services, and the developer teams themselves to make sure every title meets Balor Games' quality bar and platform certification requirements before it ships.
Key Responsibilities include but not limited to:
• Own QA strategy and standards across Balor Games' published portfolio, adapting scope and approach to each title's genre, platform mix, and risk profile.
• Oversee day-to-day management of the external QA vendors (FQA, CQA, LQA, compatibility) supporting each title in Balor Games’ portfolio, including vetting and onboarding new vendors as needed.
• Scope QA requirements against Production and developer-team milestones; book and track vendor Statements of Work (SOWs), quotes, and SOW end dates.
• Manage QA vendor budgets, purchase orders, and invoicing; flag variances against approved budgets.
• Serve as the primary QA liaison to Balor Games' external developer teams across the portfolio, aligning each studio's build/patch cadence with vendor testing cycles.
• Perform hands-on QA testing on titles as needed, including verifying fixes and writing clear, actionable bug reports.
• Provide detailed gameplay feedback to developer teams, benchmarked against comparable titles in the market.
• Review and prioritize bug reports and test results coming out of vendor QA passes; triage severity, drive fixes with developer teams, and participate in decisions around milestone acceptance and ship/no-ship quality calls in partnership with Production.
• Serve as the main point of contact for data-driven reporting on each title’s game state, quality risks, and development trajectory, in partnership with Production and leadership.
• Track platform certification and compliance requirements (PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo, Steam, mobile storefronts) and ensure vendor testing plans cover them ahead of submission deadlines.
• Maintain a current view of vendor capacity, specialties, rate cards, and performance; monitor quality and delivery, manage escalations and resolution, and match the right vendor to each title and testing phase.
• Build and maintain QA documentation, test plans, bug-tracking workflows, and reporting templates that scale across a growing, multi-developer portfolio.
Qualifications:
• 5+ years of experience in QA leadership, vendor/partner management, or production within the video game industry, including direct oversight of external QA vendors.
• Demonstrated experience managing vendor SOWs and quotes for QA services.
• Strong working knowledge of FQA, CQA, and LQA testing methodologies, bug-tracking tools, and platform certification/compliance requirements across major consoles, PC, and mobile.
• Proven ability to create, review, and refine test plans for games across a range of genres and modes, such as single-player vs. multiplayer and RPG vs. FPS.
• Proven ability to manage QA across multiple concurrent titles and external studios, with project management skills to coordinate differing vendor pipelines, tools, and deadlines.
• Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with internal teams, external developer studios, and QA vendors.
• Relationship management skills with the ability to build and maintain internal and external partnerships.
• Self-motivated with experience working independently and with a team, while being comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities.
• Proficiency with bug-tracking/test-management tools, spreadsheets, and project tracking tools.
Bonus Points:
• Avid gamer with broad knowledge of current titles across PC, console, and mobile.
• Existing relationships with FQA/CQA/LQA vendors in the games industry.
• Experience with platform partner programs (PlayStation Partners, Xbox ID@Xbox/Partner, Nintendo Developer Portal).
• Experience working with indie or mid-size external developer studios.
• Passion for process improvement and cross-functional collaboration.
We are an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected category.

The best developers don’t wait for a customer to tell them something’s broken.
They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly’s whole reason to exist. Now that agents write and ship more and more code, they can carry that instinct too. Agents write, run, and maintain the monitoring setup that guards production, while developers stay in control. Everything is defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, and versioned and reviewed like everything else that ships. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.
AI agents are shipping more code than any team can review, and reliability is lagging behind. Checkly closes this gap. As a Support Engineer, you’ll support our most valuable customers, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password on that journey.
In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel. We’re a remote-first startup that is low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love actually listening to and working with customers, working async, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in!
We care about building a team where people of all backgrounds are encouraged to do their best work. To achieve this we built a flexible and async-first startup environment with inclusive benefits and full transparency about how we pay.
## What you’ll do
Support has always been about solving real problems for real people. What’s changing at Checkly is how we do it: AI lets us automate routine work and assist us with troubleshooting, so we can go deeper on hard cases and bring what customers tell us straight back to the product. Here’s where you come in:
• Resolve customer issues. Debug Playwright tests (flaky selectors, timeouts, auth flows). Dig into API check failures with packet captures (PCAPs), traceroutes and timing breakdowns. Set up single sign-on (SSO) and SAML. When it’s a bug, bring engineering a clean reproduction, or open the pull request (PR) yourself.
• Build an outstanding AI support process. Our internal and external support agents already resolve 80% of tickets. You’ll help lift the bar: what the agent answers, when it hands off to a human, and how good those answers are.
• Turn tickets into product. Spot patterns across customers and bring product and engineering a reproduction. Your work becomes bug fixes and features.
• Own the docs. If you’ve answered something twice, it belongs in the docs and in the agent, so customers and AI get the same right answer.
• Work with modern tooling. We are continuously updating our workbench, and you’ll have modern tools like Plain, Linear, and Mintlify.

• Want a clear process for every situation before you act.

• See AI tools as something you’ll get around to eventually.

We are looking for a Senior Quality Engineer at Credo AI is a senior software engineer in test who helps the whole engineering organization ship higher-quality software. You build the testing frameworks, tooling, and fast, reliable test feedback that engineers rely on, and you work across our Elixir, TypeScript, and Python codebases to get good testing practices adopted.
This is an enablement role, not a gatekeeping one. You won't test everything yourself; you'll design the systems, set the patterns, and coach the practices that let engineers own quality with confidence. Success looks like teams that ship reliably and independently because the tools and workflows you've built make the right approach the straightforward one.
You'll work hands-on as an engineer — composing testing solutions from in-house and third-party frameworks, hardening CI/CD quality gates, writing production-quality code, and documenting the patterns and playbooks others rely on — while partnering with our Quality Engineering Lead to execute and evolve our automated testing strategy. • You've designed and implemented automated testing across unit, integration, API, and end-to-end layers, composing solutions from both in-house and third-party frameworks.

• You understand quality as an engineering discipline and prefer enabling teams to own it over centralizing testing.
• You operate well with autonomy in an early-stage startup environment.
• You have an interest in AI governance and responsible AI.
## Expectations
• Partner with the Quality Engineering Lead to execute and evolve Credo AI's automated testing and quality engineering strategy.
• Compose, build, and maintain the testing frameworks, tooling, libraries, and supporting documentation that make high-quality software the default.
• Use AI and agentic coding tools to extend our testing framework, debug tests, and build AI-enabled workflows for test authoring.
• Advance automated testing maturity across our Elixir, TypeScript, and Python codebases, keeping our practices current with industry standards.
• Strengthen CI/CD pipelines and quality gates so engineering teams get fast, actionable feedback.
• Improve the developer experience around testing so that quality is easier to build in than to skip.
• Influence and coach engineers on testing strategy and effective use of frameworks and tooling, building shared ownership of quality.
• Participate in engineering reviews focused on testability, reliability, observability, and maintainability.
• Define and track quality metrics — automation coverage, test reliability, release confidence, and defect escape rates — and use them to prioritize the highest-impact work.

The expected base salary range for this position is $140,000-$160,000. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for the position in the specified location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

While this is a remote role and we're a fully distributed team, we routinely meet up in-person. At Credo AI we value diversity, equity, and inclusion as core principles in our work environment, and the development of our product offerings, and we have implemented initiatives to foster and support these values.

Tonic.ai has been de-identifying sensitive data since 2018, and hundreds of enterprises use our products, among them eBay, American Express, UnitedHealth Group, Volvo, Qualcomm, and Commonwealth Bank. Most of them came to us with the same problem: their engineers need realistic data to build and test software, and they can’t use production data to do it.
We’re looking for someone who loves to solve complex customer problems and then immediately turns around and builds a system so that this problem solves itself next time. Moreover, this person gets to the root of why and how each customer is using Tonic so that they can maximize the value every customer is getting out of our product. The ideal Solutions Architect will be proactive, coming up with creative solutions if customers aren't getting what they need, and pressing customers when they're not doing what they need to succeed.
## Why This Role, Why Now
AI has made writing code nearly free. Knowing whether that code, and the agents built on top of it, will behave in production hasn’t gotten any easier. Agents especially need realistic, messy, data to be tested against, and basic solutions / AI slop won’t surface the failures that matter. Teams are shipping faster than their test data can keep up, and that gap is our business.
The platform is robust and scalable. What makes it valuable is someone who can walk into a customer’s environment, work out where Tonic fits in their stack and their release process, prove it in a pilot, and make it stick after the deal closes. That’s this job. You’ll work alongside our AEs before the sale and with customers’ engineering teams after it, with a direct line back to our product and engineering teams.
## What You’ll Do
• Run technical discovery with prospects’ engineering, DevOps and QA teams. Map their data sources, environments and release process, and find where Tonic fits.
• Design and demo the solution, and handle the hard technical questions: security review, deployment model, performance at scale, and how Tonic fits their CI/CD.
• Scope pilots with clear, written success criteria, then run them to a decision.
• Own onboarding after the deal closes. Deploy Tonic, connect data sources, configure de-identification and subsetting, and get the customer generating usable test data within our time-to-generation targets.
• Design test-data pipelines for agent and software testing, combining de-identified production data and synthetic data to fit each customer’s environment.
• Diagnose problems as they appear: broken foreign keys, schema drift, sensitive columns missed, jobs that won’t finish. Fix them where you can. Where you can’t, understand the issue well enough to explain it clearly to the engineer who can.
• Train customer teams so they can run Tonic without you.
• Bring field insight back to product and engineering: which features matter, which bugs are blocking deals and where the product should go next.
• Support existing customers on high-complexity issues, and work with account teams to spot expansion early.
• Turn every one-off fix into something reusable: scripts, documentation, runbooks and product improvements, so each SA can support more customers than the last.
## What We’re Looking For
• A bachelor’s degree in a technical field (computer science, engineering, information systems, math or similar), or equivalent experience.
• 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Technical Customer Success or Forward Deployed Engineer.
• Hands-on experience with relational databases and data warehouses, and with cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure or GCP). You can read a schema and tell quickly where the trouble will be.
• Working knowledge of how modern software gets built and tested: CI/CD, Docker and Kubernetes, test environments and testing frameworks.
• Comfort scripting and automating in Python and SQL. You’d rather build the fix than repeat the workaround.
• AI-native workflow. AI tools and agents are central to how you work. You know where they’re reliable and where they need your oversight.
• Ownership. You’ll often be the technical lead on an account, making sound calls without waiting to be told.
• Range. You can go deep with a DBA on one call and make the business case to a VP of Engineering on the next.
• Willingness to travel up to 25%, domestic and international.
## Nice to Haves
• Experience with agent evaluation and testing.
• Experience with test data management, data masking, or synthetic data tooling.
• Experience supporting security and compliance reviews in regulated industries like healthcare and financial services.
• Experience at an early-stage company or on a new product line.
## What Success Looks Like
In your first month, you’ll learn the platform and the delivery process and run pre- and post-sale engagements alongside your peers. By the end of your first quarter, you’ll run engagements on your own, and the scripts and runbooks you’ve written will have made your third onboarding faster than your first. After that, it’s about execution: converting pilots into customers and getting them live on time. You’ll also help shape how the SA function scales as we grow.
## Why Join
• You’ll be early in agent testing, a market that’s taking shape right now, working with some of the largest companies in the world.
• You’ll see an unusually wide range of technical environments, from startups to the Fortune 500 and from cloud-native stacks to mainframes.
• You’ll have a direct line from what you see in the field to what gets built.
• You’ll help define how the next generation of software and agents gets tested.
• Competitive compensation and equity.

About the Role
mpathic provides independent, multidisciplinary evaluations of healthcare AI technologies seeking deployment in real-world clinical settings. As part of our work supporting Utah's Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy (OAIP) regulatory sandbox, we are recruiting experienced machine learning (ML) and data science professionals to serve as technical reviewers on expert evaluation panels.
In this role, you will independently assess the technical evidence supporting healthcare AI applications, including model performance, validation methodology, generalizability, reliability, and proposed monitoring and safeguards. Your assessments will help inform recommendations regarding whether and under what conditions an AI technology may be appropriate for pilot deployment.
You will work alongside clinical and other subject-matter experts to evaluate whether applicants' technical claims are supported by credible evidence and whether their proposed evaluation and monitoring plans are appropriate for the intended healthcare setting and patient population.
This is an evaluation and scientific review role, not a model development position. We are looking for experts who can critically assess existing evidence, identify limitations, and communicate actionable recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
What You'll Be Doing
Responsibilities may include:
• Evaluate model performance and validation: Assess the appropriateness of validation methods, reference standards, sample sizes, statistical analyses, performance metrics, operating thresholds, and reported uncertainty.
• Assess data quality and representativeness: Review whether training, testing, and validation datasets are appropriate for the intended clinical application, including potential data leakage, subgroup performance differences, and generalizability across patient populations and healthcare settings.
• Evaluate technical reliability: Assess evidence of model robustness, reproducibility, known failure modes, and performance under atypical or out-of-distribution inputs.
• Review proposed evaluation plans: Determine whether applicants have established scientifically defensible methods, performance benchmarks, and success criteria for evaluating AI technologies during pilot deployment, particularly when pre-deployment evidence is limited.
• Assess technical safeguards and human oversight: Evaluate whether proposed technical safeguards, escalation mechanisms, and human-in-the-loop processes are operationally feasible and supported by appropriate testing.
• Evaluate monitoring and change management: Assess applicants' plans for detecting performance degradation, monitoring model behavior, managing updates, and establishing criteria for intervention or rollback.
• Collaborate with multidisciplinary reviewers: Work alongside clinicians and other technical experts to identify concerns that require cross-disciplinary judgment, particularly where model performance may affect clinical outcomes.
• Produce structured evaluation findings: Document strengths, limitations, missing evidence, and technical concerns using a standardized review framework. Provide clear, evidence-based recommendations and identify what additional evidence or changes would resolve identified concerns.
• Participate in reviewer calibration and quality assurance: Contribute to discussions intended to improve consistency, transparency, and defensibility across evaluations.
• Maintain independence and confidentiality: Follow conflict-of-interest, confidentiality, and data-handling requirements when reviewing proprietary or unpublished materials.
What We're Looking For
We are seeking technically rigorous, independent reviewers who can distinguish between a promising technology and evidence that adequately supports its proposed use.
Strong candidates are comfortable questioning unsupported performance claims, identifying limitations in study design, and recognizing when additional evidence is needed before meaningful conclusions can be drawn. They understand that healthcare AI evaluation is context-dependent: technical performance must be considered alongside the intended population, clinical application, degree of autonomy, and potential consequences of model error.
Candidates should also be able to translate complex technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for multidisciplinary audiences, including clinicians and state regulatory stakeholders.
Basic Qualifications
• At least 3 years of professional or applied research experience in machine learning, data science, biostatistics, clinical informatics, or a closely related field, with direct experience evaluating or validating predictive models or AI systems.
• Demonstrated understanding of model evaluation methodologies, including appropriate performance metrics, validation design, statistical uncertainty, threshold selection, and common sources of bias or methodological error.
• Experience assessing model performance on independent or held-out data and interpreting whether reported performance generalizes beyond the evaluation dataset.
• Hands-on experience evaluating at least one relevant class of AI systems, such as clinical natural language processing, large language models, conversational AI, medical imaging, computer vision, or tabular predictive models.
• Ability to critically assess technical research, evaluation reports, or validation studies and identify methodological limitations or unsupported conclusions.
• Strong analytical writing skills, including the ability to communicate complex findings clearly to non-technical audiences.
• Ability to work independently while contributing to multidisciplinary expert review and calibration processes.
• Willingness to complete confidentiality agreements, conflict-of-interest disclosures, and reviewer training requirements.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience evaluating AI or ML systems used in healthcare, clinical decision support, digital health, or other high-stakes environments.
• Familiarity with clinical AI evaluation and reporting frameworks, such as TRIPOD+AI, STARD-AI, CONSORT-AI, DECIDE-AI, or model cards.
• Experience evaluating generative AI, LLM-based systems, or autonomous AI agents, including multi-turn behavior, reliability, hallucinations, and technical safeguards.
• Experience with robustness testing, adversarial evaluation, red teaming, or systematic failure-mode analysis.
• Knowledge of production monitoring, distribution shift, model drift, version control, and change-management practices.
• Experience designing or evaluating human-in-the-loop systems or comparing model performance against human expert judgments.
• Familiarity with FDA guidance for AI-enabled medical devices, clinical decision support, or software as a medical device.

## About the role:
Cresta’s AI Receptionist answers the phone for small businesses that would otherwise miss the call. It handles millions of conversations a month today, making sure no call goes unanswered and helping owners complete the front-office tasks that keep their business running, and it does so across hundreds of customers. Whether those conversations are actually good is the single most important question in the business, and it deserves a full-time owner. That’s you.
As our first AI Agent Evaluation Engineer, you define what quality means for every agent we run, you build the systems that measure it across every conversation, and you are the person the company trusts when the question is “how good is it, really?”
The work combines hands-on conversation analysis, rigorous evaluation design, and engineering execution: reading and annotating real conversations to learn how the agent actually fails, building the automated evaluation systems (LLM-based judges, golden sets, regression suites) that measure those failures at scale, and keeping those systems honest by calibrating them against human judgment. Fixing what you find is welcome but not the core of the job; an accurate, prioritized picture of agent quality is.
What You'll Do :
## Evaluation Design & Quality Definition
• Define and maintain the evaluation rubric for the agent across three axes: adherence (did it follow its design, call the right tools, respect guardrails), outcome (did the conversation achieve its goal), and conversation experience (latency, turn-taking, tone, repetition).
• Write the annotation guidelines and failure taxonomy the team uses to talk about failures precisely; run calibration sessions and measure inter-rater agreement.
• Classify and prioritize failure modes by severity and frequency so engineering and product work on what matters most.
## Conversation Analysis & Annotation
• Review production conversations by hand every week, leverage QA partners; open-code failures, cluster them, and turn the clusters into the evaluations worth automating.
• Trace each failure to its likely cause (prompt, knowledge gap, tool or flow bug, speech recognition) and route it to the right owner with enough evidence to act on.
• Evaluate across languages and report quality by segment (language, accent, audio quality, intent), not just in aggregate.
## Scalable Evaluation Systems
• Build and operate the evaluation pipeline that scores every production conversation, combining automated checks, LLM-based judges, and human review.
• Calibrate every automated judge against human labels before trusting it; treat judge error as the primary measurement risk.
• Design sampling strategies (stratified by intent, language, caller type, audio conditions) so that reported changes in quality are real.
• Build and maintain the golden set and regression suite that every prompt, model, knowledge, and flow change is validated against before release.
## Coverage & Edge Cases
• Maintain the failure-mode coverage map: which behaviors are tested, partially tested, or unmeasured; close the gaps.
• Design evaluations for behaviors no standard harness covers: high-stakes conversation types such as handoffs to a human, misuse and unwanted-caller handling, and resilience under upstream failures.
• Define the quality and latency thresholds the agent is held to.
## Reporting & Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Report quality trends to internal stakeholders and customers clearly, with uncertainty stated and without burying bad news.
• Partner with forward-deployed engineers, backend engineers, product managers, and the voice/language engineering team to turn findings into prioritized recommendations.
• Document methodology so results are reproducible and the evaluation practice outlives any one person.
## What We're Looking For:
• 3+ years of professional experience in software engineering, applied ML, or data-intensive research roles, including at least 1–2 years working hands-on with LLM-based systems in production.
• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computational Linguistics, Cognitive Science, Statistics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
• Built and operated an end-to-end evaluation system for a production LLM product (agent or otherwise): rubric, human labels, automated judge, regression suite.
• Deep understanding of evaluation methodology: what golden sets, judges, regression suites, and calibration are for, and when each fails. Tool-agnostic; you will work in our in-house tooling.
• Fluent in how LLM agents work: prompts, tool calls, context handling, multi-turn state. You can read a trace and tell what the agent was doing and why.
• Strong programming skills in Python and experience with LLM APIs; able to build and ship evaluation tooling independently. Fine-tuning and ML frameworks are not required.
• Able to write a rubric that independent reviewers would score the same way, and to measure whether they do.
• Able to design a test from an open-ended quality question: you decide what to measure and how, rather than executing a predefined plan.
• Willing to do non-scalable work weekly, both yourself and by directing our QA partners: listening to calls, labeling conversations, building a failure taxonomy from scratch.
• Professional fluency in at least one language other than English, sufficient to evaluate multilingual agent behavior directly.
• Strong written communication; you author the guidelines others follow.
Note on Our Hiring Process
We highly value your time and engineering craftsmanship. To ensure a streamlined and objective process, the first step for qualified applicants following an initial resume review is a self-paced CoderPad technical assessment. This allows you to showcase your practical coding and problem-solving skills in a real-world environment before moving into conversational interview rounds.

This role allocates approximately 80% of its scope to comprehensive Content QA—auditing creative assets from initial ideation through regulatory review, followed by rigorous testing within Salesforce Marketing Cloud (SFMC), cross-client rendering environments, and live deployment validation to guarantee alignment with technical documentation, design specs, dynamic messaging logic, and WCAG standards.
The remaining 20% involves partnering with Technical QA Analysts to conduct data schema audits, HTML structure reviews, and deployment file verifications. Working closely with cross-functional partners across creative, engineering, and project management, you will track, triage, and resolve issues in Mantis within a high-velocity enterprise ecosystem where precision and compliance are paramount.
This role will report to the Sr. Director of Development & QA.
## What You'll Accomplish
## Content QA: Creative Proofing (Primary)
• Proof every creative round before client delivery: full end-to-end reviews in early rounds, targeted checks of legal and compliance edits in later rounds.
• Ensure accuracy in spelling, grammar and punctuation, and enforce brand guidelines and the client's email design system.
• Verify each round reflects all client feedback, with no unintended changes.
• Confirm terms, conditions and disclosures are complete before legal review.
• Document proofing feedback clearly in Workfront using the team's proofreading checklist.
## Content QA: Email Testing (Primary)
• Test coded emails in the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Sandbox against the user story, approved creative and test plan.
• Validate copy, images, links and tracking across every version and audience.
• Confirm personalized and dynamic content renders correctly for each test record, including Movable Ink elements.
• Verify accessibility against WCAG 2.1 AA, including alt text and ARIA labels tested with a screen reader.
• Run render tests across devices and email clients using Email on Acid and Inbox Monster.
• Log clear, reproducible bugs in Mantis and verify fixes before closing them.
• Support live production testing in the week before deployment, often with same-day turnarounds.
## Technical QA Support (Secondary)
• Help audit the mail plan, user story and test data before development begins.
• Assist with HTML code reviews: template use, link URLs, alt text, ARIA labels, heading structure, fonts, subject lines and preheaders.
• Review final file packages for completeness and naming conventions before hand-off to Salesforce.
• Help validate accessibility and logic fixes, and back up the Technical QA Analyst during peak periods.
## Team and Process
• Join internal creative reviews and developer handoffs to flag content and testing risks early.
• Attend daily scrum and weekly QA resource planning, and keep Workfront tasks and timesheets current.
• Contribute to retrospectives and help improve QA checklists, test plans and workflows.
What You Bring
## Experience & Expertise
• 2–4 years focused on editorial review, creative verification, or marketing quality assurance within client-facing agency networks or corporate environments.
• Direct operational experience validating responsive HTML communications, predominantly across Salesforce Marketing Cloud or equivalent enterprise campaign execution tools.
• Background supporting highly regulated sectors such as banking, insurance, or health, managing multi-tier governance workflows and legal sign-offs.
• Practical understanding of WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility guidelines, including alt tags, ARIA attributes, and semantic document markup.
• Proven history auditing real-time dynamic content and audience personalization against technical briefs, user criteria, and test scenarios.
• Proficiency documenting, routing, and managing issue remediation within corporate ticket management platforms like Mantis, Jira, or Azure DevOps.
## Skills & Capabilities
• Exceptional attention to detail, with strong command of grammar, spelling, punctuation and style guides.
• Ability to read basic HTML well enough to inspect links, alt text, heading tags and font declarations.
• Comfort with email render and testing tools such as Email on Acid, Litmus or Inbox Monster.
• Ability to use a screen reader (VoiceOver, NVDA or JAWS) to verify accessible content.
• Clear, concise written communication, especially bug reports that a developer can act on without a follow-up call.
• Strong organization and prioritization across several concurrent projects with shifting deadlines.
• Proficiency with Google Workspace and spreadsheets, for working with test plans, data files and change logs.
## Mindset
• Accountability: you own your QA sign-off and treat every missed error as a learning opportunity, not someone else's problem.
• Learning: you are curious about the technical side of email and eager to grow your skills toward Technical QA.
• Teamwork: you see QA as a partner to creative and development, not a gatekeeper, and you jump in when others are at capacity.
• Candor: you give direct, kind and specific feedback, and you ask questions early rather than assume.
• Composure: you stay calm and methodical during Live Testing crunches and same-day turnarounds, with compliance top of mind.
## Nice to Haves
• Salesforce Certified Marketing Cloud Email Specialist or similar certification.
• Familiarity with AMPscript, personalization strings or dynamic content logic.
• Experience with Movable Ink or other real-time email personalization platforms.
• Exposure to automated accessibility audit tools such as Deque axe.
• Experience with Adobe Workfront, Basecamp or Figma.
• Knowledge of financial services or payments terminology, card product marketing or Card Member lifecycle communications.
What We Offer
• Competitive compensation aligned with your experience and impact
• Remote flexibility
• Collaborative culture that values diverse perspectives and innovative thinking
• Work that makes a measurable difference for your clients

Millennium is proud to be part of the Markon enterprise, a network of specialized organizations united in support of critical national security missions. Millennium is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate or allow discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, citizenship, disability, veteran status or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law.
## Responsibilities
Millennium Corporation is hiring a Software Test Engineer to work 100% REMOTE . The candidate must have an active secret clearance.
Duties -
• Manages the planning, design, execution and reporting for software tests. May supervise junior testers.
• Provides administrative support by reviewing business / software requirements and provides inputs on requirement gaps, testability, and methodology.
• Provides administrative support by reviewing program documentation and products for quality and adherence to design concepts.
• Assists in preparing milestone status reports and deliveries/ presentations on the system concept to colleagues, end user representatives.
• Supports coordination of Cybersecurity T&E IAW DoDI 5000.02 and the DoD Risk Management Framework.
• Prepare / review test plans.
• Prepare test cases, test scripts and analyzes test data and ensures traceability to requirements.
• Works with the software development group throughout the development process.
• Supports the software configuration management process and understands all software components and their interface requirements.
• Performs software testing at all levels from module or unit testing through all levels of software integration testing and user acceptance tests (manual / automated).
• Reports defects and tracks defects and their status throughout the defect management process.
• Analyze test results and track software testing metrics.
• Supports the test lead with the creation of test reports.
• Train, mentor and supervise junior software engineers.
## Qualifications
• Candidate must have an active secret clearance.
• BS & 8 yrs of experience or HS Diploma and 13 yrs of experience.
• Required -Security+ certification. AWS Cloud practitioner cert preferred.
## Business Development
Assist with Business Development activities as required to support Millennium's strategic business objectives, which may include but not limited to participation in technical interviews, creation of technical documentation, general proposal writing support and proposal color reviews.
## Physical Requirements
• Must be comfortable with prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
• Must be able to lift up to 10-15 pounds at a time.
## Travel Requirements
<10%
## COMPENSATION:
$115,000-$120,000
The salary range provided for this position is intended as a general guideline and does not guarantee a specific salary or compensation amount. Final compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors, including, relevant education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities.

## Overview
Job Title: GIS Software Quality Assurance Engineer Location: Remote
Mano Lani LLC is seeking an experienced Senior GIS Software QA Engineer to support a U.S. Army program focused on improving the accuracy, reliability, and consistency of installation geospatial and Real Property data.
This position is ideal for a hands-on software quality assurance professional with experience testing GIS applications, validating complex datasets, and ensuring that automated tools produce accurate, repeatable results.
The role supports the development and testing of ArcGIS-based tools, GIS and Real Property data reconciliation workflows, automated validation processes, and geospatial web applications used by Army installation personnel.
The ideal candidate combines strong software testing expertise with practical knowledge of Esri GIS technology, database validation, and test automation. They are comfortable investigating complex data issues, identifying the root causes of software defects, and working closely with GIS specialists, developers, and Real Property analysts to deliver reliable technical solutions.
Key Responsibilities
-Develop, document, and execute comprehensive software test plans, test cases, and testing procedures for GIS applications and automated workflows.-Perform functional, regression, integration, and data validation testing to identify software defects and determine their causes.-Test ArcGIS Pro tools, geoprocessing workflows, GIS data validation processes, and automated reporting solutions.-Validate the accuracy and integrity of spatial data, geodatabase attributes, field values, and relationships between GIS and Real Property records.-Test automated business rules designed to identify, correct, and flag inconsistencies in GIS datasets.-Verify the accuracy of automated Real Property Unique Identifier (RPUID) corrections, missing-attribute population, and exception reporting.-Test GIS–Real Property alignment tools, automated workbooks, reports, dashboards, and web mapping applications.-Use SQL, scripts, or other testing methods to compare source data with application outputs and confirm data accuracy.-Document defects with clear reproduction steps, expected results, actual results, and supporting evidence.-Collaborate with developers, GIS analysts, and Real Property specialists to troubleshoot defects and verify corrections.-Support the development of repeatable and automated testing processes to improve software reliability and reduce manual testing effort
## Requirements
Required Qualifications
-Education: Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in a relevant field of study.-Software quality assurance: Experience developing and executing software test plans to identify software problems and their causes.-Technical expertise: Experience and knowledge across key technical tasks and high-impact assignments, with the ability to serve as a technical expert across multiple assignments.-Esri GIS knowledge: Understanding of Esri ArcGIS application software.-Army Real Property and GIS knowledge: Understanding of DoD and Army Real Property and Installation Geospatial Information and Services (IGI&S) policies and guidance.-GIS standards: Understanding of the most recently published DCS G-4 IGI&S Quality Assurance Plans (QAPs) and the current Spatial Data Standard for Facilities, Infrastructure and Environment (SDSFIE) Army Adaptation.-CAC eligibility: Ability to obtain a Department of the Army Common Access Card (CAC).-Hands-on experience testing software applications, including GIS-enabled applications, geospatial workflows, or spatial data processing tools.-Experience creating and executing test cases, documenting defects, conducting regression testing, and verifying software fixes.-Practical knowledge of ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Online, or comparable enterprise GIS environments.-Experience validating database records, application outputs, and complex datasets using SQL or equivalent data-querying methods.-Ability to test automated data transformations, business rules, field calculations, and reporting workflows.-Experience with automated testing, scripting, or repeatable data validation processes.-Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to distinguish software defects from source-data quality issues.
Preferred Qualifications
-Testing Esri ArcGIS applications, geoprocessing tools, Python/ArcPy scripts, or GIS automation workflows.Working with enterprise geodatabases, spatial databases, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, SQL Server, or Oracle.-Developing automated tests using Python, Selenium, pytest, Postman, or similar tools.-Testing APIs, ETL pipelines, system integrations, web GIS services, and dashboards.-Supporting Army installations, DPW, IGI&S, facilities management, infrastructure, or Real Property systems.-Familiarity with HQIIS, RPUID, GIS–Real Property reconciliation, and Real Property data quality requirements.-Experience testing applications where data accuracy, traceability, and compliance with defined business rules are critical.
Benefits: Mano Lani LLC offers a comprehensive benefits package including a liberal vacation plan, a matching retirement program, and competitive salaries commensurate with skills and experience. For more information about our organization, please visit our web site at www.manolani.com.
Physical Requirements: Work may involve sitting or standing for extended periods of time. Position may require typing and reading from a computer screen. Must have sufficient mobility, including but not limited to bending, reaching, and kneeling to complete daily duties in a timely and efficient manner. There is a possibility that due to parking availability and location of work, walking moderate to long distance may be required. Possible lifting up to 25 lbs.
Please note: Mano Lani LLC reserves the right to change or modify job duties and assignments at any time. The above job description is not all encompassing. Positions functions and qualifications may vary depending on business needs.

AI coding agents are part of how we work every day, and we invest in getting good at using them. We’re also careful with them, because customers run their content operations on Rally. We’re tracking industry trends and innovations, but using our day-to-day experiences to separate signal from noise.

About This Role
As a Quality Engineer at BibleProject, you empower teams to ship reliable, secure, and performant software by embedding quality practices throughout the development lifecycle. You lead with automation and observability, design for testability, and partner with Engineers, Product, and Design to shift quality left so that defects are prevented, not just detected. You'll design, build, and own the app's automation suite, identify where coverage is needed across the test pyramid and partner with engineers to close the gaps, and use production signals to target risk — bringing demonstrated experience driving quality for production software at scale.
The App squad owns the BibleProject mobile app, where our audience reads and studies Scripture, often in community. Quality is what makes that experience trustworthy, and mobile makes that its own kind of challenge: the app has to hold up offline or on a weak connection, across a wide range of iOS and Android devices. You'll be the quality owner and anchor for this squad, working independently and shaping how we build for quality early rather than waiting to be handed test cases. That matters especially right now: we're building toward the future of the app, and testability is still something we can shape as we go. Manual testing here is targeted exploratory discovery — the critical and edge cases, the accessibility gaps, the things automation won't catch — rather than high-volume regression.
Most importantly, you'll be an integral part of maturing the product engineering culture of BibleProject, setting and maintaining a high bar with regard to our standards and people, and working to create an environment where great technical professionals like yourself can ship work worthy of our mission at a sustainable pace that reflects the BibleProject values: creative, humble, thoughtful, unifying, generous, and unhurried.
Core Functions
Leadership
Own the App squad's automation suite and quality roadmap independently — build, maintain, and evolve it without ongoing pairing support.
Own test strategy across the pyramid: identify where tests are needed — unit, component, integration, end-to-end — and partner with engineers to close gaps, influencing scope and sequencing based on risk and user impact.
Champion shift-left practices: drive testability in design reviews and codify quality engineering standards and patterns.
Partner with Product, Design, DevOps, and Data to define testable acceptance criteria (usability, accessibility, offline/edge-case behavior) and align on SLOs and release readiness.
Drive continuous improvement: identify bottlenecks in CI/CD, observability, and environments, and deliver measurable fixes.

Build and maintain the automation suite with durable patterns, stable test data, and reliable test environments across iOS and Android.
Track coverage gaps as the product evolves, and partner with engineers to get unit and component-level tests written and maintained in the codebase.
Integrate tests into CI/CD with clear gates, fast feedback, and actionable reporting, driving down flaky failures over time.
Plan and execute targeted exploratory testing on critical flows, new designs, and edge cases — offline/poor-connectivity behavior, accessibility gaps, and other issues automation won't catch — documenting reproducible steps and user impact.
Establish, track, and improve quality signals (defect rate, change-failure rate, test stability, coverage depth, crash-free rate); validate releases using production signals and lead post-release verification for high-risk launches.

Mobile test automation: hands-on building and maintaining mobile UI automation suites from durable, maintainable patterns rather than one-offs; experience with Appium and the Page Object Model is a plus.
Observability and analysis: using logs, metrics, traces, and crash reporting to validate behavior and identify defects quickly.
Mobile quality judgment: offline and poor-connectivity correctness, behavior across a wide device range, mobile performance budgets and their user impact, and the release constraints of shipping through app stores.
Product fluency for mobile: fluent in iOS and Android conventions, able to identify and articulate why something that technically passes still violates expected user experience.

• Design, develop, and maintain advanced simulators for IP and serial tactical data link terminals, radios, navigation systems, and sensors.
• Contribute to the definition and ongoing verification of minimum system requirements for JRE's full range of deployment platforms.
• Refactor JRE code for testability, introducing API, RPC, and messaging seams to enable additional white- and gray-box testing.
• Mentor developers, testers, and less-experienced test engineers in test automation best practices as we expand automated coverage across the codebase.
• Optimize the performance and quality of our test automation suites.
• Quarantine, troubleshoot, and fix nondeterministic tests.

## About Practifi (The Real Story)
Practifi is the only intelligent CRM company that meets wealth management firms wherever they are in their AI adoption journey. Our enterprise-grade, compliance-first foundation brings client data, workflows, and relationship intelligence together in one system, so firms can understand what matters, take the right action, and scale without ever needing a new CRM.
That same directness runs through how we work. We're a team of fewer than 100 people, remote-first across the US and Australia, and we'd rather tell you how this job actually works than polish it for the pitch. We don't sell a version of the role that doesn't exist.
## The Opportunity (What This Role Really Means)
When a wealth management firm moves onto Practifi, the first thing they judge us on is their data. If a household is missing a member, if a client shows up twice, or if a servicing team points to the wrong advisor, they notice on day one. So do their clients.
Right now, quality assurance on those data migrations is handled by whoever is delivering the engagement, on top of everything else on their plate. It works, but it means every client gets a slightly different process and nobody has a clear view of the issues that keep coming back.
We're creating this role to change that. As our Data QA Analyst, you'll be the dedicated owner of data migration quality across every client onboarding engagement. You'll work the checklist object by object, build one standard the whole team uses, and spot the patterns a single-project view misses. You'll be a big part of why a client's first login feels like their business, not a spreadsheet import.
## Your Day-to-Day (The Honest Version)
The Core Work
• Validate every migration end to end. You'll analyze source data (record counts, missing values, duplicates, orphaned contacts, inconsistent values), then walk through the Practifi interface object by object to confirm everything displays and connects the way the client's Data Mapping Document says it should.
• Check the details that matter. Every record carries a valid External Id and Batch Id, nothing is owned by a default system user, every contact is tied to at least one relationship, and counts reconcile to source or have a clear explanation.
• Log, route, and retest. You'll capture screenshots of failed checks, log findings in Asana and JIRA, route fixes to engineering, and retest once they're corrected.
• Report clearly. After each Initial Load and Final Load, you'll give the Project Manager, Consultant, or Business Analyst the metrics they need, and you'll prepare the final QA sign-off report before go-live.
• Raise the flag early. When a data issue puts a go-live at risk, you'll escalate it to the Project Manager within 24 hours
• Build the standard. You'll own one QA checklist and issue-tracking format for every engagement, replacing the client-by-client workbooks in use today, and you'll track recurring issues across clients so we fix the process, not just the record.
The Reality Check
The Practifi data model has its own vocabulary, and it takes time to learn how it all fits together. You won't figure it out alone. You'll complete the same onboarding and training curriculum as every individual contributor here, including our PractifiU learning platform, and you'll have a Practibuddy mentor from day one.
You'll also be working alongside Consultants, Business and Data Analysts, Data Engineers, and Project Managers. Part of the job is raising problems in a way that keeps projects moving. And when QA volume is lighter, you'll flex into delivery support, so you'll see the whole implementation, not just your portion of it.
The Growth
This is a new role, which means you'll shape it. The checklist, the reporting format, and the process improvements you contribute each quarter become part of how Data Services operates.
You'll earn a Salesforce certification once you're here, with time and support built in, and an annual Learnbucks stipend for the courses and certifications you choose after that. We promote from within. A role that sees every engagement is a strong foundation for a path into consulting, data engineering, or delivery leadership.
## What We're Really Looking For
The Must-Haves
• 3 to 5 years of experience in data quality, data migration, data validation, or quality assurance, ideally in a CRM or software environment
• Hands-on experience reconciling data: comparing record counts, running field-by-field checks, and finding duplicate and orphaned records
• Comfort working inside Salesforce or a comparable CRM, navigating objects, records, and related lists
• A working understanding of how relational data fits together (IDs, lookups, and records that link other records)
• Experience logging and tracking issues in JIRA, Asana, or a similar tool
• Clear written communication, including findings a non-technical stakeholder can act on
The Nice-to-Haves
• Experience with Salesforce Inspector, the Salesforce Developer Console, Data Loader, or SOQL queries
• Background in wealth management, financial services, or another regulated industry
• Experience supporting client onboarding or software implementation projects
• Strong spreadsheet skills (lookups, pivot tables, conditional formatting)
A Salesforce certification isn't required to apply. You'll earn one with us.
The More Important Stuff
• You’re observant and tuned into the details within the data.
• You care about the cause of an issue, not just the fix.
• You're comfortable telling a Project Manager something they don't want to hear, and you do it early and kindly.
• You like building structure where there isn't any yet.
• You're honest about what you don't know and curious enough to go find out.
## What Taking This Leap Gets You
The Practical Stuff
• Base salary: $78,000 to $95,000. We share the range because you deserve to know it before you apply. Where you land depends on your experience against the role.
• Generous time off: 20 days of paid vacation, 10 sick days, 3 personal days, and 3 volunteering days annually
• Medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance benefits, plus a 401(k) with company match
• Fully remote within the US
The Cultural Stuff
• A Practibuddy mentor from your first day, so you always have someone to ask
• An annual Learnbucks education stipend for the courses and certifications you choose
• Bi-annual in-person summits in Chicago where the whole company gets together
• A Slack culture where questions are welcome and wins get celebrated
• Remote-first that's real: genuine work-life integration, not a line in a job ad
## Living Our Values Daily
• Growth: You'll be part of building a function from the ground up, with Learnbucks and a real promotion path behind you.
• Collaboration: You'll partner with every delivery role on every engagement, and the fix is always a team effort.
• Transparency: The salary is in this ad, and your QA findings will be shared openly, good news and bad.

Build the product capabilities that help ensure AI-enabled healthcare experiences are useful, trusted, and responsibly deployed.
At Wolters Kluwer Health, the UpToDate suite supports millions of clinical decisions every day. As AI becomes part of healthcare workflows, quality cannot be treated as a one-time launch checkpoint. AI experiences need to be evaluated, monitored , and improved continuously so clinicians and care teams can trust the information and interactions they rely on.
As Senior Product Manager, AI Quality & Evaluation , you will play a core role in translating clinical quality standards and evaluation strategy into scalable product capabilities. Working under product leadership and in close partnership with clinical, technical, and data experts, you will help define the requirements, workflows, tooling, automation, and reporting needed to evaluate AI-enabled experiences before and after launch.
This role does not own the clinical quality standard or statistical methodology . It helps make those standards operational at scale through usable tools, repeatable workflows, measurable signals, and clear evidence that supports product decisions, customer trust, and responsible AI.
What You'll Do
• Translate expert-defined quality standards and evaluation methods into product requirements, workflows, and roadmap priorities.
• Drive discovery and delivery for defined AI quality and evaluation capabilities, including tooling, automation, monitoring, evidence capture, and reporting.
• Partner with clinical, data science, engineering, product, legal, compliance, and customer-facing teams to operationalize AI evaluation before and after launch.
• Identify opportunities to automate and scale evaluation workflows while preserving appropriate expert oversight.
• Define product requirements for review workflows, issue triage, launch readiness, post-launch monitoring, and quality reporting.
• Use evaluation insights to inform product improvements, user experience, content quality, model behavior, and operational processes.
• Track emerging market practices and customer expectations related to AI quality, evaluation, benchmarking, and responsible AI.
• Translate AI quality and evaluation practices into clear narratives for product leaders, customer-facing teams, and internal stakeholders.
What You'll Bring
• 5+ years of product management experience in healthcare, enterprise SaaS, data-driven products, platform products, quality, or related areas.
• Strong product discovery and execution skills, including requirements definition, roadmap planning, experimentation, and metrics-driven decision-making.
• Ability to translate complex clinical, technical, quality, or risk concepts into practical product requirements and workflows.
• Experience working with engineering, data, clinical, compliance, customer-facing, or operational stakeholders.
• Strong analytical thinking and comfort defining metrics, dashboards, workflows, and decision criteria.
• Strong communication skills, especially around quality, trust, tradeoffs, evidence, and customer value.
• Curiosity and learning agility around AI, evaluation methods, responsible AI, and emerging technologies.
Preferred Background
• Experience with AI-enabled products, healthcare technology, quality tooling, data products, search/retrieval quality, content quality, clinical validation, or decision-support products.
• Familiarity with AI evaluation methods, benchmarks, monitoring, human-in-the-loop review, automation, or applied machine learning concepts.
• Experience in healthcare, clinical workflows, regulated environments, or professional-information products.
• Experience supporting customer-facing narratives around product quality, trust, or responsible technology.
What Success Looks Like
• Expert-defined quality standards are translated into scalable product workflows, tools, and requirements.
• Evaluation processes become more automated, repeatable, measurable, and usable by cross-functional teams.
• Product teams have clearer quality signals and launch-readiness criteria for AI-enabled experiences.
• Evaluation insights improve product quality, customer trust, user experience, and responsible AI practices.
